title: Ethernet RS(544,514) "KP4" FEC: encoder and decoder at 32 symbols (320 bits) per clock, one codeword in 17 clocks, with syndrome, riBM, two-pass Chien / Forney correction and uncorrectable-codeword marking

regs.name: CTRL
regs.desc: Decoder options (taken when a codeword reaches the correction pass)

fields.desc: bypass correction: the data passes unchanged and every codeword with a non-zero syndrome is reported bad
bypass indication: uncorrectable codewords are not marked on DEC_OUT.d_out_bad (the UNCORR interrupt still fires)

regs.name: ENC_IN
regs.desc: Encoder input beat: 32 message symbols (beats 0..15) or 2 (beat 16, symbols 0..1); writing the last word sends it

fdesc.e_in_first: beat 0 of a codeword (realigns the beat counter)

regs.name: ENC_OUT
regs.desc: Encoder output beat: the message passed through, beat 16 with the 30 parity symbols in symbols 2..31; reading the last word pops it

regs.name: DEC_IN
regs.desc: Decoder input beat: 32 received symbols; writing the last word sends it

fdesc.d_in_first: beat 0 of a codeword (realigns the beat counter)

regs.name: DEC_OUT
regs.desc: Decoder output beat: the corrected symbols; reading the last word pops it

fields.desc: symbols corrected in the last codeword that reached the correction pass

irqs.name: UNCORR
irqs.desc: an uncorrectable codeword (with correction bypassed: a codeword with errors)

irqs.name: ERESYNC
irqs.desc: ENC_IN beat 0 (first) in the middle of a codeword: the partial codeword was dropped

irqs.name: DRESYNC
irqs.desc: DEC_IN beat 0 (first) in the middle of a codeword: the partial codeword was dropped

features: RS(544,514) over GF(2^10) (x^10 + x^3 + 1), g(x) = prod (x - alpha^j), j = 0..29, t = 15: the IEEE 802.3 clause 91 / 119 / 172 "KP4" FEC codeword used by 100G..1.6T Ethernet.
32 symbols (320 bits) per clock in and out of both encoder and decoder: one codeword every 17 clocks, at full rate with back-to-back codewords.
Encoder: systematic, one clock of latency; the parity update for a whole beat is one GF(2)-linear map.

Decoder: syndromes, reformulated inversionless Berlekamp-Massey (two iterations per clock), a Chien pass that counts the roots (uncorrectable when the LFSR length is above 15 or the roots are not as many), a Chien / Forney pass that corrects; a 4-codeword buffer; 36 clocks from the last beat in to the first beat out.

Uncorrectable codewords marked on every beat (d_out_bad), correction and indication bypass, per-codeword events and corrected-symbol count, realignment on first, ready / valid flow control that holds the pipeline.
notes: Through the registers a beat is 11 words: data bits 32k .. 32k + 31 in word k = 0..9 (symbol s is bits 10s .. 10s + 9), then first (and bad) in word 10. The data path is meant to be wired to the PCS directly; the registers serve set-up, status and test.

The 400GBASE-R PCS around the FEC (256b/257b transcoding, scrambling, alignment markers, the 2-way codeword interleaving) is the Ethernet_PCS IP, built on two of these cores. Not implemented: the clause 45 statistics counters (they count the CORR / UNCORR events and STATUS.st_nsym), and the reduced-latency path of correction bypass.
Throughput: 320 bits per clock carry 302 message bits (514 / 544); one instance at 1 GHz is about 302 Gb/s of FEC payload, so 800G needs three instances (four with interleaving) and 1.6T six (eight).
sequence: Set CTRL (both bypasses 0 for normal operation); enable the interrupts wanted.
Encode: write 17 beats to ENC_IN (first set on beat 0), reading ENC_OUT after each beat (ENC_IN is held while ENC_OUT is full).
Decode: write 17 beats to DEC_IN; the corrected codeword comes out of DEC_OUT, 17 beats, about 36 clocks after the last beat in; CORR / UNCORR and STATUS.st_nsym report it.
verification: Test vectors (tb/Ethernet_RS_FEC_vec.hex, `make -f Makefile.Ethernet_RS_FEC vec` rebuilds them) from the reference model scripts/ethfec/rs_ref.py, whose encoder matches the reedsolo library: clean codewords, single errors at both ends, bursts, 1..15 random errors, 15 errors in the parity, errors at beat boundaries, 16..200 errors and a word with an LFSR length above 15. Every message is encoded and every received word decoded and compared.

Loopback with random messages and 0..40 random symbol errors, back-to-back codewords at full rate (the output must come out back-to-back, at the fixed latency), random input gaps and output back-pressure, both bypasses, realignment, and a reset with codewords in flight.

The core checker has its own GF(2^10), generator polynomial, symbol-serial LFSR encoder and a classic Berlekamp-Massey / Chien / Forney decoder with a syndrome check of the result, and compares every beat out of the encoder and decoder, the events and the symbol count; plus the ready / valid rules and the stage occupancy the 17-clock schedule relies on.
